P5/hang.analysis: P9.9 addendum (a66224a, 4 in 60 min): a resumable session over the canonical copy of a refused valid map ran the map streak's tskip past the copy's stop into stale bytes, uncharged (seed 7001290:130 alone: 94 s, 158 s CPU). Fixed by D367; in a worker's sequence the stall also reproduced at 7002434:219 on the pre-fix tree and not after. A hang depends on the worker's state (buffers reused across cases), so replay it in sequence from its worker's start, not only with --replay, and measure CPU, not wall time: the campaign machine is often loaded. A new occurrence is a new finding until replayed.

P2/valid-roundtrip/reencode/text.analysis: P9.9 addendum (seed 7002107, index 27; 15 occurrences on a66224a): d81847668efb1c976081, a tag-24 payload holding invalid UTF-8, decodes under valid (D358: the payload need only be well-formed) but the JS Writer and the wasm SDK's encoder scanned the payload alone under the full profile and refused it with text. Fixed: they scan the whole tag item, so the payload gets decode's rule (well-formed under valid, a valid item with tag24 'valid' and under deterministic/Bindle); Rust's Writer already checked the whole message. Since the addendum the re-encode signature carries the refusal's code (P2/valid-roundtrip/reencode/<code>): a cause other than this one is a new signature, not this triage. History: before the addendum the signature was P2/valid-roundtrip/reencode, triaged 'fixed, D348' for the normalised-bignum key collision (a200f6c240f6), whose duplicate_key/normalized refusal the property accepts and never reports.
